requirements.quote:
The GOAWAY frame also contains a 32-bit error code (Section 7) that
   contains the reason for closing the connection.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a GOAWAY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Include and process a 32-bit error-code field that gives the reason for closing the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The presence and width of the error-code field can be inspected in serialized and parsed GOAWAY frames.

requirements.quote:
Endpoints MAY append opaque data to the frame payload of any GOAWAY
   frame.  Additional debug data is intended for diagnostic purposes
   only and carries no semantic value.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint sends or receives a GOAWAY frame containing payload data after the required fields.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit appended opaque diagnostic data and treat it as having no protocol-semantic value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not derive protocol behavior or semantics from the appended debug data.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can supply or emit trailing opaque bytes and verify they are accepted without affecting protocol decisions.

requirements.quote:
security- or privacy-sensitive data.  Logged or otherwise
   persistently stored debug data MUST have adequate safeguards to
   prevent unauthorized access.
requirements.condition: When GOAWAY debug data is logged or otherwise stored persistently.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply safeguards adequate to prevent unauthorized access to the stored debug data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not persist debug data in a form accessible without adequate authorization safeguards.
requirements.why_checkable: Storage configuration and access-control tests can verify that persisted debug data is protected from unauthorized access.

requirements.quote:
The WINDOW_UPDATE frame (type=0x08) is used to implement flow
   control; see Section 5.2 for an overview.
requirements.condition: When encoding or dispatching a WINDOW_UPDATE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use frame type value 0x08.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame type octet can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
Both types of flow control are hop by hop, that is, only between the
   two endpoints.  Intermediaries do not forward WINDOW_UPDATE frames
   between dependent connections.  However, throttling of data transfer
   by any receiver can indirectly cause the propagation of flow-control
   information toward the original sender.
requirements.condition: When an intermediary receives a WINDOW_UPDATE frame on one connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the update only to the hop on which it was received.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not forward the WINDOW_UPDATE frame to a dependent connection.
requirements.why_checkable: An intermediary integration test can observe whether received WINDOW_UPDATE frames are copied onto dependent connections.

requirements.quote:
Flow control only applies to frames that are identified as being
   subject to flow control.  Of the frame types defined in this
   document, this includes only DATA frames.
requirements.condition: When accounting for flow control among frame types defined by this document.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply flow-control accounting to DATA frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply flow-control accounting to other frame types defined by this document.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can send each defined frame type and inspect whether flow-control windows change.

requirements.quote:
document, this includes only DATA frames.  Frames that are exempt
   from flow control MUST be accepted and processed, unless the receiver
   is unable to assign resources to handling the frame.
requirements.condition: When a receiver receives a frame exempt from flow control and can assign resources to handle it.
requirements.required_behavior: Accept and process the frame regardless of flow-control-window availability.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject or defer the frame merely because flow-control credit is unavailable.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust flow-control windows, send an exempt frame, and verify normal processing.

requirements.quote:
is unable to assign resources to handling the frame.  A receiver MAY
   respond with a stream error (Section 5.4.2) or connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR if it is unable to accept
   a frame.
requirements.condition: When a receiver cannot accept a frame because it cannot assign resources to handling it.
requirements.error_behavior: The receiver may respond with either a stream error or a connection error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Resource-failure injection can verify that either permitted error scope uses FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.

requirements.condition: When serializing or parsing a WINDOW_UPDATE frame header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 24-bit Length field as 0x04.
requirements.why_checkable: The header's 24-bit length field can be inspected directly.

requirements.condition: When serializing or parsing a WINDOW_UPDATE frame header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 8-bit Type field as 0x08.
requirements.why_checkable: The header's 8-bit type field can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote: Unused Flags (8),
requirements.condition: When serializing or parsing a WINDOW_UPDATE frame header.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the flags field as an 8-bit unused field.
requirements.why_checkable: The flags field width and handling can be checked from the encoded header and parser behavior.

requirements.quote:
Reserved (1),
     Stream Identifier (31),
requirements.condition: When serializing or parsing the stream identifier in a WINDOW_UPDATE frame header.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the field as one reserved bit followed by a 31-bit stream identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Bit-level serialization and parsing can verify the field layout.

requirements.quote:
Reserved (1),
     Window Size Increment (31),
requirements.condition: When serializing or parsing a WINDOW_UPDATE payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the payload as one reserved bit followed by a 31-bit Window Size Increment.
requirements.why_checkable: The four-byte payload's bit layout can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
WINDOW_UPDATE frame is one reserved bit plus an unsigned 31-bit
   integer indicating the number of octets that the sender can transmit
   in addition to the existing flow-control window.  The legal range for
   the increment to the flow-control window is 1 to 2^31-1
   (2,147,483,647) octets.
requirements.condition: When decoding or applying a valid WINDOW_UPDATE payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the 31-bit unsigned integer as an increment of 1 through 2^31-1 octets to the existing flow-control window.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interpret it as an absolute window size or as a signed value.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary-value frames can verify unsigned parsing, additive semantics, and the stated legal range.

requirements.quote: The WINDOW_UPDATE frame does not define any flags.
requirements.condition: When implementing WINDOW_UPDATE flag semantics.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the frame as defining no flags.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assign WINDOW_UPDATE-specific semantics to flag bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can vary flag bits and verify that no WINDOW_UPDATE behavior is selected from them.

requirements.quote:
The WINDOW_UPDATE frame can be specific to a stream or to the entire
   connection.  In the former case, the frame's stream identifier
   indicates the affected stream; in the latter, the value "0" indicates
   that the entire connection is the subject of the frame.
requirements.condition: When a WINDOW_UPDATE frame has a nonzero stream identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the increment to the flow-control window of the identified stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply it as a connection-level update.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send an update with a nonzero identifier and inspect which window changes.

requirements.quote:
The WINDOW_UPDATE frame can be specific to a stream or to the entire
   connection.  In the former case, the frame's stream identifier
   indicates the affected stream; in the latter, the value "0" indicates
   that the entire connection is the subject of the frame.
requirements.condition: When a WINDOW_UPDATE frame has stream identifier 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the increment to the connection flow-control window.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply it to an individual stream window.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send an update on stream 0 and inspect which window changes.

requirements.quote:
A receiver MUST treat the receipt of a WINDOW_UPDATE frame with a
   flow-control window increment of 0 as a stream error (Section 5.4.2)
   of type PROTOCOL_ERROR; errors on the connection flow-control window
   MUST be treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1).
requirements.condition: When a receiver gets a stream-specific WINDOW_UPDATE frame whose increment is 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or apply the zero increment.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat it as a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted stream WINDOW_UPDATE with a zero increment permits direct observation of the emitted stream error and code.

requirements.quote:
A receiver MUST treat the receipt of a WINDOW_UPDATE frame with a
   flow-control window increment of 0 as a stream error (Section 5.4.2)
   of type PROTOCOL_ERROR; errors on the connection flow-control window
   MUST be treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1).
requirements.condition: When a receiver gets a connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE frame whose increment is 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or apply the zero increment.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat it as a connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted stream-0 WINDOW_UPDATE with a zero increment permits direct observation of connection termination.

requirements.quote:
WINDOW_UPDATE can be sent by a peer that has sent a frame with the
   END_STREAM flag set.  This means that a receiver could receive a
   WINDOW_UPDATE frame on a stream in a "half-closed (remote)" or
   "closed" state.  A receiver MUST NOT treat this as an error (see
   Section 5.1).
requirements.condition: When a WINDOW_UPDATE frame is received on a stream in the half-closed (remote) or closed state.
requirements.required_behavior: Accept the state/frame combination without reporting an error merely because of the stream state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat receipt of the WINDOW_UPDATE in either stated stream state as an error.
requirements.why_checkable: State-machine tests can place a stream in either state, inject WINDOW_UPDATE, and observe whether an error is generated.

requirements.quote:
A receiver that receives a flow-controlled frame MUST always account
   for its contribution against the connection flow-control window,
   unless the receiver treats this as a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1).  This is necessary even if the frame is in error.
requirements.condition: When a receiver receives a flow-controlled frame and does not treat the frame as a connection error.
requirements.required_behavior: Account the frame's contribution against the connection flow-control window, including when the frame otherwise has an error.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit connection-window accounting merely because the frame has an error.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can inject erroneous flow-controlled frames and inspect connection-window accounting.

requirements.quote:
A WINDOW_UPDATE frame with a length other than 4 octets MUST be
   treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a receiver receives a WINDOW_UPDATE frame whose payload length is not 4 octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not process it as a valid WINDOW_UPDATE frame.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat it as a connection error of type FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed frames with shorter and longer payload lengths can verify the connection-level error and error code.

requirements.quote:
Two flow-control windows are applicable: the stream flow-control
   window and the connection flow-control window.  The sender MUST NOT
   send a flow-controlled frame with a length that exceeds the space
   available in either of the flow-control windows advertised by the
   receiver.
requirements.condition: When a sender is about to send a nonempty flow-controlled frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure the frame length fits within both the applicable stream window and the connection window advertised by the receiver.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send the frame if its length exceeds the available space in either window.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can set distinct stream and connection credits and verify that transmission is blocked whenever either is insufficient.

requirements.quote:
receiver.  Frames with zero length with the END_STREAM flag set (that
   is, an empty DATA frame) MAY be sent if there is no available space
   in either flow-control window.
requirements.condition: When both flow-control windows have no available space and a zero-length DATA frame has END_STREAM set.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the empty END_STREAM DATA frame to be sent.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust both windows and verify that the zero-length END_STREAM frame is still allowed.

requirements.quote:
For flow-control calculations, the 9-octet frame header is not
   counted.
requirements.condition: When calculating a frame's contribution to flow-control windows.
requirements.required_behavior: Count the flow-controlled payload length without the 9-octet frame header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not deduct the 9-octet frame header from flow-control windows.
requirements.why_checkable: Window deltas after sending or receiving frames can be compared with payload length and total wire length.

requirements.quote:
After sending a flow-controlled frame, the sender reduces the space
   available in both windows by the length of the transmitted frame.
requirements.condition: After a sender sends a flow-controlled frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Reduce both the applicable stream window and the connection window by the transmitted frame's flow-controlled length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reduce only one of the two windows or leave either unchanged.
requirements.why_checkable: The two window values can be inspected before and after transmission.

requirements.quote:
The receiver of a frame sends a WINDOW_UPDATE frame as it consumes
   data and frees up space in flow-control windows.  Separate
   WINDOW_UPDATE frames are sent for the stream- and connection-level
   flow-control windows.
requirements.condition: When a receiver consumes received data and chooses to restore both stream-level and connection-level flow-control space.
requirements.required_behavior: Send separate WINDOW_UPDATE frames for the stream window and the connection window.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not combine both window updates into one WINDOW_UPDATE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: An integration test can consume buffered data and inspect the identifiers and number of emitted WINDOW_UPDATE frames.

requirements.quote:
A sender that receives a WINDOW_UPDATE frame updates the
   corresponding window by the amount specified in the frame.
requirements.condition: When a sender receives a valid WINDOW_UPDATE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Increase the corresponding stream or connection window by the increment specified in the frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not replace an existing window with the increment or update a non-corresponding window.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can establish a known window, inject an update, and inspect the resulting corresponding window.

requirements.quote:
A sender MUST NOT allow a flow-control window to exceed 2^31-1
   octets.
requirements.condition: Whenever a sender updates or maintains a stream or connection flow-control window.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the flow-control window at or below 2^31-1 octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not allow the window to exceed 2^31-1 octets.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary tests can apply increments near the maximum and inspect the stored window value and resulting control action.

requirements.quote:
octets.  If a sender receives a WINDOW_UPDATE that causes a flow-
   control window to exceed this maximum, it MUST terminate either the
   stream or the connection, as appropriate.  For streams, the sender
   sends a RST_STREAM with an error code of FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR; for the
   connection, a GOAWAY frame with an error code of FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR
   is sent.
requirements.condition: When a WINDOW_UPDATE would cause a stream flow-control window to exceed 2^31-1 octets.
requirements.required_behavior: Terminate the affected stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply the overflowing increment and continue the stream normally.
requirements.error_behavior: Send RST_STREAM with error code FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A boundary-value update can force stream-window overflow and the emitted RST_STREAM and code can be observed.

requirements.quote:
octets.  If a sender receives a WINDOW_UPDATE that causes a flow-
   control window to exceed this maximum, it MUST terminate either the
   stream or the connection, as appropriate.  For streams, the sender
   sends a RST_STREAM with an error code of FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR; for the
   connection, a GOAWAY frame with an error code of FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR
   is sent.
requirements.condition: When a WINDOW_UPDATE would cause the connection flow-control window to exceed 2^31-1 octets.
requirements.required_behavior: Terminate the connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply the overflowing increment and continue the connection normally.
requirements.error_behavior: Send GOAWAY with error code FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A boundary-value stream-0 update can force connection-window overflow and the emitted GOAWAY and code can be observed.

requirements.quote:
Flow-controlled frames from the sender and WINDOW_UPDATE frames from
   the receiver are completely asynchronous with respect to each other.
requirements.condition: When flow-controlled frames and WINDOW_UPDATE frames cross in transit.
requirements.required_behavior: Handle their transmission and receipt asynchronously without requiring lockstep alternation or acknowledgment ordering between them.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not require a WINDOW_UPDATE exchange to be synchronized with each individual flow-controlled frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Concurrency tests can reorder and overlap data and WINDOW_UPDATE traffic and verify continued correct window accounting.
